authority: founder act, 2026-11-08 ("Yes, freeze them") — S3 Class-B precedent

suites.ws-work-continuity: Part A · honest reading of replayed history (laws A1a…A6, defeat candidates DC-1…DC-8)
suites.ws-work-read-scope: Part B · standing, revocable Work reading scope (laws T1…T11, defeat candidates DC-1…DC-15)
suites.ws-decision-continuity: settled-decision record (laws L1a…L7b, defeat candidates DC-1…DC-14)

law: Implementation fails suite -> repair the implementation. Editing a frozen law, contract, or defeat candidate requires a formal, named founder act with evidence the LAW or the INSTRUMENT was wrong — never that an implementation was inconvenient.
additive_law_permitted: New law may be ADDED at its own address with its own falsifiers and defeat candidates. Adding never edits a frozen file; a frozen file's blob hash is the mechanical test.

deliberately_not_frozen.tests/constitutional/*/matrix.test.ts an: the runners; extending them to run additional laws does not weaken the law they run
deliberately_not_frozen.tests/constitutional/*/dynamic/**, dynam: physical witnesses of an implementation, not the law
deliberately_not_frozen.lib/**, app/**, database/migrations/**: the implementation and migration candidates the suites judge

limits: The reference doubles in the contract files are test doubles, never seeds. Freezing the suites does not authorize merging, applying the migrations, or deploying. A frozen law can be later found wrong; the path is a named founder act, not an edit.
note: Blob hashes, not a commit diff: they survive history rewriting and say exactly which bytes are law.
